The paper develops an adaptive Hessian-based non-stationary Gaussian process response surface method.
The method aims to approximate expensive-to-evaluate probability density functions, particularly those arising from Bayesian solutions of large-scale inverse problems.
The key challenge is that the posterior probability distribution is often non-Gaussian and expensive to evaluate due to the nonlinearity of the parameter-to-observable map.
The method constructs a piecewise Gaussian approximation tailored to the local Hessian of the negative log probability density.
Gaussian process machinery is used to combine the local Gaussian approximations into a global analytical response surface.
The non-stationary covariance function combines local Laplace approximations using Hessian-informed membership probabilities.
An adaptive sampling strategy is used to select training points in high probability regions of the parameter space.
Standard Gaussian process response surfaces use stationary covariance functions that cannot adapt to variable smoothness.
The Hessians appear in the kernel functions and membership probabilities to guide the covariance function construction.
The proposed method is demonstrated on several example problems, including inverse shape electromagnetic scattering in 24-dimensional parameter space.
